; AMD GPU targets this solver ships native code objects for.
;
; SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH, on the same terms as cuda/cuda_arch.txt beside it.
; Every consumer derives from this file and nothing restates the list:
;
;   * the Makefile beside it, which is the Linux build path,
;   * the Windows native build,
;   * ppf-cts-core's SUPPORTED_GFX, generated by its build.rs, which is the
;     gate check_gpu() applies before a run starts,
;   * the shipped-architecture text the solver prints when it rejects a device.
;
; A build file that names a target instead of deriving it here fails the solver
; build: arch_literal_guard in ppf-cts-solver/build.rs walks every Makefile and
; .bat under the compute source and the native Windows build and rejects
; anything after --offload-arch= that is not a variable expansion.
;
; Comments use ';' because cmd.exe's `for /f` treats it as end-of-line by
; default, so a .bat reads this file with no extra filtering. Blank lines are
; skipped by every consumer.
;
; A consumer that cannot read this file, or that parses no target line from it,
; must fail loudly rather than proceed on an empty list. An empty list would
; build a library with no device code and reject every GPU at run time, and both
; failures would point away from the missing file that caused them.
;
; WHY GENERIC TARGETS AND NOT A PART LIST. An AMD code object carries no forward
; compatibility between gfx numbers: each is its own ISA, so there is no
; analogue of CUDA's `floor`. A `gfxN-generic` target emits ONE code object that
; runs on any member of its family, at the cost of instructions the family does
; not share. Six generic lines therefore cover the range that enumerating parts
; would spend forty-six on. Measured 2026-09-14 on HIP 7.15 / amdclang 23: all
; six generic targets are accepted by `hipcc --offload-arch=` and each emits a
; code object the offload bundler finds.
; DERIVE THE COUNT FROM THIS FILE rather than repeating it: the list
; below is now longer than those six.
;
; AND TWO SPECIFIC PARTS, BECAUSE NO GENERIC TARGET COVERS THEM. gfx908 (MI100)
; and gfx90a (MI200) are gfx9 parts that `gfx9-generic` does NOT include:
; measured 2026-09-15 from the toolchain's own generic-target table, that family
; is gfx900, gfx902, gfx904, gfx906, gfx909 and gfx90c and nothing else
; (generic_targets.txt beside this file records the source and the commit). A
; generic line can therefore not reach them, and a bare `gfxNNNN` target, which
; covers exactly itself, is the only way to ship code for them. Both are accepted
; by `hipcc --offload-arch=` and each emits a code object the offload bundler
; finds, checked the same way the six generic ones were.
;
; THEY COST BUILD TIME IN PROPORTION. Every target is a full compile of every
; generated entry, so eight targets is a third more work than six, and the figure
; to watch is the per-target compile rather than the link.
;
; WHY NO `dcgpu` TARGET IS HERE, AND WHY ADDING ONE IS THE THING TO REFUSE.
; AMD publishes the datacenter families (gfx94X, gfx950, gfx125X) for Linux and
; NOT for Windows. Every target listed below ships on both. So this file is one
; list read by both builds exactly as long as no Linux-only target enters it; a
; dcgpu line would fork it per platform, which is a different and larger change
; than adding a target.
;
; gfx908 AND gfx90a ARE INSTINCT PARTS AND DO NOT BREAK THAT RULE, which is worth
; stating because they look like the case the paragraph above refuses. The rule
; is about what AMD ships per PLATFORM, not about Radeon versus Instinct: AMD
; publishes gfx908 and gfx90a distributions for Linux AND Windows, while the
; `dcgpu` families are Linux-only. So this stays one list.
;
; BOTH WAVE WIDTHS ARE IN THIS LIST. gfx9 and gfx9-4 are 64-lane families and
; the gfx10, gfx11 and gfx12 families are 32 under HIP's default. The neutral
; kernel that ballots reads `compute::simd_width` and types its lane mask from
; `compute::ballot_t` rather than assuming either, which is what makes one list
; possible.
;
; target  One offload target passed to --offload-arch. A `gfxN-generic` target
;         emits one code object for a whole family; a bare `gfxNNNN` emits one
;         for exactly that part, and is used only where no generic target
;         covers it.

target gfx9-generic
target gfx9-4-generic
target gfx10-1-generic
target gfx10-3-generic
target gfx11-generic
target gfx12-generic
target gfx908
target gfx90a
